title: Enterprise Platform Architecture
summary: Architecting a composable enterprise platform across frontend capability ownership, independently structured backend services and reliable asynchronous processing.

problem.context: A long-lived process platform needed to support independently evolving business capabilities without allowing UI composition, service integration and background processing to become tightly coupled.
problem.statement: How can an enterprise platform evolve by capability while keeping ownership and dependency direction explicit?
constraints: Business capabilities must remain independently understandable and maintainable.
Frontend composition cannot rely on duplicated route, navigation or permission configuration.
Services must integrate without direct cross-service data access.
Background processing must tolerate retries and controlled shutdown.

process.title: Map capability boundaries
process.description: Identify where UI features, business rules, persistence and asynchronous responsibilities should be owned.

process.title: Define dependency rules
process.description: Set explicit direction across frontend layers and Domain, Application, Infrastructure and API boundaries.

process.title: Standardize foundations
process.description: Turn recurring integration, metadata and worker concerns into reusable contracts and libraries.

decisions.title: Micro Frontend with Feature-Sliced Design
decisions.rationale: Organize React and TypeScript by business capability while keeping host, module, feature and shared responsibilities visible in the codebase.
decisions.tradeOff: More boundary discipline and contract management in exchange for clearer ownership and safer independent evolution.

decisions.title: Metadata-driven composition
decisions.rationale: Co-locate route, navigation, permission and registration metadata with the capability that owns it, then generate shared contracts.
decisions.tradeOff: A stricter metadata schema is required, but duplicated configuration and composition drift are reduced.

decisions.title: .NET Microservices with Clean Architecture
decisions.rationale: Keep business rules independent from transport and persistence while assigning each service a clear capability boundary.
decisions.tradeOff: Additional layers and mapping are accepted to protect domain behavior and long-term maintainability.

decisions.title: Contract-led service integration
decisions.rationale: Use an API Gateway, shared contracts and typed clients so integrations remain explicit without sharing service-owned data access.
decisions.tradeOff: Contract evolution needs version discipline, but coupling stays visible and testable.

decisions.title: Reliable RabbitMQ workers
decisions.rationale: Model automation, document processing and notification work as asynchronous handlers with explicit execution policies.
decisions.tradeOff: Eventual completion replaces synchronous simplicity, requiring idempotency and operationally safe worker behavior.

solution.title: Frontend Architecture
solution.description: A composable React platform where capabilities own their features and metadata.

solution.title: Backend Architecture
solution.description: Owned .NET services structured around domain behavior and explicit application use cases.

solution.title: Platform Engineering
solution.description: Reusable mechanisms for tenant-aware persistence, asynchronous work and repeatable delivery.

outcomes.title: Explicit ownership
outcomes.description: Frontend capabilities and backend services have defined responsibility boundaries instead of implicit shared behavior.

outcomes.title: Deterministic composition
outcomes.description: Generated metadata contracts keep routes, navigation, permissions and module registration aligned.

outcomes.title: Reusable foundations
outcomes.description: Typed clients, contracts and platform libraries standardize recurring engineering decisions without centralizing business ownership.

outcomes.title: Retry-safe processing
outcomes.description: Workers are designed around idempotency, controlled concurrency, cancellation and graceful shutdown.

learnings: A shared foundation remains maintainable only when its ownership and extension points are explicit.
Frontend modularity depends on dependency rules and metadata contracts, not directory structure alone.
Service boundaries are protected as much by data-access rules as by API contracts.
Reliable asynchronous processing begins with execution semantics, not only message transport.

title: Multi-channel Customer Engagement Platform
summary: Delivering an embedded customer communication experience across multiple channels with clear integration boundaries and repeatable environment delivery.

problem.context: A customer-facing product needed an embedded chat experience, multiple communication entry points and a delivery path that behaved consistently across environments.
problem.statement: How can multiple communication tools feel like one product without turning integrations into product-wide coupling?
constraints: The chat experience needed to remain embeddable in an existing marketing surface.
Third-party and open-source capabilities required explicit adapter boundaries.
Channel-specific behavior could not leak across the whole application.
UAT and production delivery needed the same containerized foundation.

process.title: Separate product and integration concerns
process.description: Keep the landing experience and embedded widget independent from provider-specific configuration.

process.title: Define channel boundaries
process.description: Treat Web and social channels as adapters with their own connection and delivery concerns.

process.title: Make delivery repeatable
process.description: Containerize the product and use CI/CD to promote the same foundation across environments.

decisions.title: Embedded widget boundary
decisions.rationale: Keep customer communication reusable and independently embeddable instead of binding it to a single page implementation.
decisions.tradeOff: The widget needs a stable integration contract, but product surfaces remain easier to change.

decisions.title: Adapter-led channel integration
decisions.rationale: Contain Chatwoot, Dify/RAG and channel-specific concerns behind explicit integration points.
decisions.tradeOff: Adapters add mapping work while preventing provider behavior from spreading through the product.

decisions.title: Container-first delivery
decisions.rationale: Use the same Docker foundation and CI/CD workflow for UAT and production releases.
decisions.tradeOff: Delivery configuration becomes part of engineering ownership, improving environment consistency.

solution.title: Product Experience
solution.description: A focused marketing surface with an embedded chat entry point.

solution.title: Integration Layer
solution.description: Explicit adapters for conversation tooling, assisted responses and customer channels.

solution.title: Delivery Foundation
solution.description: A repeatable path from integration work to deployable environments.

outcomes.title: Reusable communication entry point
outcomes.description: The embedded widget can be integrated without coupling the entire product surface to provider details.

outcomes.title: Contained integration behavior
outcomes.description: Channel and provider concerns stay behind visible boundaries that can evolve independently.

outcomes.title: Consistent delivery
outcomes.description: Containerization and CI/CD provide the same release foundation for UAT and production.

learnings: Integration-heavy products stay understandable when provider behavior is treated as an adapter concern.
An embedded UI needs a deliberate contract to remain reusable across product surfaces.
Environment consistency improves when packaging and release workflows are designed with the feature.
